programme: AQA AS Physics 7407/2 Paper 2 method trainer
copyright: Original compact coaching flashcards; not reproductions of AQA question paper text.
coverage: Three exam sections, reusable question styles from available papers since 2018; deduplicated pattern practice. This is not yet a question-by-question verification of every part of every paper.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Compare a closed reading with zero.
cards.paper2Trap: A positive zero error must not be added.
cards.front: A micrometer's zero reading is +0.03 mm. What correction is made?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Think about crushing or compressing a thin sample.
cards.paper2Trap: A micrometer reading is not improved by overtightening.
cards.front: Why use the ratchet of a micrometer to close on a wire?
cards.back: To apply a consistent small measuring force.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: One point might not represent an uneven wire.
cards.paper2Trap: A single high-precision reading is not enough.
cards.front: How can you reduce error in a wire's measured diameter?
cards.back: Measure at several positions and orientations; take a mean.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Think about how a distance is obtained.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not count only one endpoint.
cards.front: For a measured length, which readings contribute uncertainty?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: The denominator is the reading, not its unit.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not divide by the uncertainty.
cards.front: How do you convert an absolute uncertainty into a percentage?
accept: delta x divided by x times 100

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Divide 0.2 by 5.0 then convert to percent.
cards.paper2Trap: 0.04 is a fraction, not 0.04%.
cards.front: If A = 5.0 ± 0.2 cm, percentage uncertainty in A?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Identify multiplication/division in the relationship.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not add absolute uncertainties with different units.
cards.front: For a product or quotient, how do fractional uncertainties combine?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Powers multiply fractional uncertainty.
cards.paper2Trap: Squaring a length does not square percentage uncertainty.
cards.front: If a diameter is squared, what happens to its percentage uncertainty?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: This is a quotient.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not subtract the uncertainties.
cards.front: If resistance R = V/I, which uncertainties contribute?
cards.back: Percentage uncertainty in V plus that in I.
accept: add percent V and percent I

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A discrepancy alone does not establish disagreement.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not compare only rounded central values.
cards.front: What is the most direct way to test whether two measurements agree?
cards.back: Compare the difference with their combined uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Consider repeated results under the same bias.
cards.paper2Trap: More repeats do not automatically remove a zero error.
cards.front: What distinguishes systematic error from random scatter?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Ask what the instrument reads when the quantity vanishes.
cards.paper2Trap: A repeat of the same nonzero reading may keep the bias.
cards.front: What is the best quick check for a suspected zero error?
cards.back: Check the instrument reading at true zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Look at the range around the data point.
cards.paper2Trap: It is not automatically the range of repeat readings.
cards.front: What does an error bar on a graph represent?
cards.back: The uncertainty interval for a plotted quantity.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Think of unpredictable variation.
cards.paper2Trap: A mean cannot remove every systematic error.
cards.front: How can random error be reduced in repeated timing measurements?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Write 2s = a t² and compare y = mx.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not put a/2 on the 2s axis.
cards.front: A graph of 2s against t² uses s = ½at². What is its gradient?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Choose an x variable that makes y = mx.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not force a straight line through y against x.
cards.front: For y = kx², what should you plot to obtain a straight line?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Rewrite the equation as y = k(1/x).
cards.paper2Trap: x itself gives a reciprocal curve.
cards.front: For y = k/x, what should the horizontal axis be?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Draw your triangle on the line, not through random points.
cards.paper2Trap: Using two adjacent noisy points exaggerates error.
cards.front: How is a graph gradient calculated with a best-fit line?
cards.back: Use a large triangle on the line: Δy/Δx.
accept: change in y divided by change in x

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Treat the gradient as y/x.
cards.paper2Trap: A gradient is not automatically unitless.
cards.front: Where should the units of a gradient come from?
cards.back: Vertical-axis unit divided by horizontal-axis unit.
accept: vertical units divided by horizontal units

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Think of lines still consistent with the bars.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not invent lines that miss error bars.
cards.front: How do you estimate the uncertainty in gradient using error bars?
cards.back: Compare steepest and shallowest acceptable gradients.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Take half the gradient range.
cards.paper2Trap: The full range 0.8 is not ± uncertainty.
cards.front: If Gmax = 8.3 and Gmin = 7.5, estimate the gradient uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Rearrange into y = mx + c.
cards.paper2Trap: Forcing the line through origin can hide a systematic effect.
cards.front: For an intercept-based practical graph, what must be checked first?
cards.back: Whether the model predicts a zero or nonzero intercept.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Multiply a vertical force by a horizontal time.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not confuse area with gradient.
cards.front: A force-time graph gives what physical quantity from area?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Rewrite as charge Q = current I × time t. The area of I–t has units of coulombs.
cards.paper2Trap: The gradient is not charge.
cards.front: An I-t graph gives what quantity from area?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Integrate velocity with sign.
cards.paper2Trap: Distance needs total positive area, not signed cancellation.
cards.front: For velocity-time data, what does the signed area give?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Try to identify y = mx + c.
cards.paper2Trap: A straight-looking sketch alone cannot prove proportionality.
cards.front: What should you do when a curved graph is requested as a linear test?
cards.back: Rearrange the relationship before selecting transformed axes.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Test the ratio predicted by the relationship.
cards.paper2Trap: Two nearby points are weak evidence.
cards.front: How do you support a claim of proportionality from data?
cards.back: Check whether the appropriate ratio is constant within uncertainty.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Which other quantity controls the resonant frequency?
cards.paper2Trap: Do not call the measured frequency a control.
cards.front: A student varies wire diameter in a standing-wave experiment. Name one key control variable.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Start from E = stress/strain.
cards.paper2Trap: A force-extension gradient alone is not Young modulus.
cards.front: When comparing materials' Young modulus, what must be recorded besides force and extension?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Reduce reaction-time fraction of one period.
cards.paper2Trap: Timing one swing increases relative uncertainty.
cards.front: How can a pendulum or oscillator period be measured more reliably?
cards.back: Time many cycles and divide by their number.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Identify what changes between repeated runs.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not assume a real apparatus is perfectly ideal.
cards.front: Why should a student specify the same starting displacement for oscillations?
cards.back: To keep a possible amplitude effect controlled.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Voltage is measured between two points.
cards.paper2Trap: An ideal voltmeter is not placed in series.
cards.front: How should a meter be connected to measure potential difference across a wire?
cards.back: Voltmeter in parallel with the wire.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: It must carry the current being measured.
cards.paper2Trap: An ammeter in parallel can short the circuit.
cards.front: How should a meter be connected to measure current in the wire?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Current causes power dissipation.
cards.paper2Trap: Heating may change R between readings.
cards.front: Why turn off current between resistivity readings?
cards.back: To reduce heating and resistivity changes.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A balanced bridge has no detector p.d.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not pick the point of maximum detector reading.
cards.front: In a bridge balance method, what indicates the null point?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Consider the size of the triangle used for a gradient.
cards.paper2Trap: More repeats at one setting do not test the trend.
cards.front: Why repeat a practical over a wide range of independent-variable values?
cards.back: To make the trend and gradient more reliable.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Which variable responds to your change?
cards.paper2Trap: Do not label the quantity under investigation as controlled.
cards.front: How is a control variable different from the dependent variable?
cards.back: It is kept fixed, not measured as the outcome.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Link equipment or method to uncertainty.
cards.paper2Trap: 'Use better apparatus' is too vague.
cards.front: What makes an experimental improvement specific enough for marks?
cards.back: Name the source of error and how the change reduces it.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A graph may have a maximum/minimum plausible gradient.
cards.paper2Trap: A small numerical difference may not be significant.
cards.front: What should you compare before claiming two gradients disagree?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Gravity acts vertically.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not use vertical acceleration in x.
cards.front: For a projectile, which motion direction has constant velocity (neglecting drag)?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Separate y motion from x motion.
cards.paper2Trap: Horizontal speed does not set fall time.
cards.front: How do you find the time of flight to a known vertical drop?
cards.back: Use vertical SUVAT with a = g.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: The horizontal component is constant, so multiply it by time: x = vₓt.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not multiply total speed by time if angled.
cards.front: What formula then gives a projectile's horizontal range?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: θ is the slope angle to horizontal.
cards.paper2Trap: mg cos θ is perpendicular to slope.
cards.front: In a slope problem, which component of weight acts down the slope?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Acceleration is zero.
cards.paper2Trap: The driving force need not be zero.
cards.front: At constant speed uphill, what is the resultant force along the slope?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Use work per time = Fv.
cards.paper2Trap: Force alone is not power.
cards.front: When a body moves at constant speed against resistance, engine power is?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Take the vertical change in GPE.
cards.paper2Trap: mgh is energy, not power.
cards.front: What equation finds work done by an upward lift through height h?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Efficiency = useful / input.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not invert the fraction.
cards.front: For efficiency, which energy or power is in the numerator?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Choose a pivot that removes unknown forces.
cards.paper2Trap: Equal forces alone do not ensure rotational equilibrium.
cards.front: An equilibrium beam supports two unequal loads. Which condition is easiest to use?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: This area is work done.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not use gradient as the energy.
cards.front: For a force graph against extension, what is the area?
cards.back: Elastic potential energy stored (up to elastic limit).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Stress divided by strain.
cards.paper2Trap: It is not Young modulus outside the linear region.
cards.front: For a stress–strain graph, what is its elastic-region gradient?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Use a common final velocity.
cards.paper2Trap: Kinetic energy need not be conserved.
cards.front: If two objects stick together, which conservation law finds their speed?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: The change in v may be much larger than one speed.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not add unsigned momentum blindly.
cards.front: For a collision with reversed direction, what sign rule matters?
cards.back: Choose one positive direction and use signed velocities.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Find area then divide by Δt.
cards.paper2Trap: Peak force is not mean force.
cards.front: For a force-time pulse, how do you obtain mean force?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Distance is never negative.
cards.paper2Trap: Signed areas give displacement, not distance.
cards.front: A velocity-time graph dips below the axis. For distance travelled, what do you do?
cards.back: Add the magnitudes of all areas.

cards.paper2Trap: Do not measure angles from the surface.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Compare integer and half-integer wavelengths.
cards.paper2Trap: Amplitude alone does not set phase difference.
cards.front: For a light interference fringe, what decides bright versus dark?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Compare with y = mx + c.
cards.paper2Trap: The negative gradient gives r, not ε.
cards.front: In an emf–current graph V = ε − Ir, which graph feature gives ε?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Rearrange V = ε − Ir.
cards.paper2Trap: The gradient itself is negative.
cards.front: What is the magnitude of gradient on a V–I source graph?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Same series current through both.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not use the upper resistance in numerator.
cards.front: In a simple series potential divider, the p.d. across the lower resistor is?
accept: Vin times lower R divided by total

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Voltage is held constant.
cards.paper2Trap: Higher resistance means lower power at fixed V.
cards.front: How do you compare two filaments' powers if supplied at same voltage?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Combine E = hf and c = fλ.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not use E = hcλ.
cards.front: How do you find emitted photon energy from wavelength?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Think E = hf − φ.
cards.paper2Trap: Intensity controls emission rate, not maximum KE.
cards.front: In photoelectric effect, what changes the maximum photoelectron KE?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: 1 eV is the charge of one electron through 1 V.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not divide by elementary charge.
cards.front: From a photon-energy change in eV to joules, do what?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: A neutron becomes a proton.
cards.paper2Trap: Nucleon number stays unchanged.
cards.front: For a beta-minus decay, what happens to proton number Z?

cards.subject: Physics

cards.paper2Skill: Section B: waves, circuits and particles
cards.paper2Hint: Distinguish it from a baryon.
cards.paper2Trap: Three quarks is a baryon.
cards.front: When identifying a meson's quark content, how many constituents?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: The radius and diameter scale together: area is proportional to diameter squared (A ∝ d²).
cards.paper2Trap: Do not assume doubled diameter means doubled area.
cards.front: MCQ: doubling a wire's diameter makes cross-sectional area how many times larger?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: At fixed resistivity and length, R = ρL/A. Area depends on diameter squared.
cards.paper2Trap: Use area, not diameter, in denominator.
cards.front: MCQ: at constant material and length, doubling wire diameter makes resistance what fraction?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Elastic strain energy is E = ½kx², so compare the squares of extensions.
cards.paper2Trap: Energy is not proportional to extension.
cards.front: MCQ: double a spring's extension in its Hooke-law region. Strain energy changes by?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Choose P = V²/R.
cards.paper2Trap: Don't use I fixed when V is fixed.
cards.front: MCQ: at unchanged voltage, resistance doubles. Power changes by?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Hold resistance fixed in P = I²R, then square the change in current.
cards.paper2Trap: Don't treat P as linear in I.
cards.front: MCQ: at unchanged resistance, current doubles. Power changes by?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: For fixed mass, KE = ½mv²: compare speed by taking a square root.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not double speed.
cards.front: MCQ: kinetic energy doubles for a fixed mass. Speed changes by?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Momentum p = mv is proportional to speed when mass is fixed.
cards.paper2Trap: Momentum is linear in v.
cards.front: MCQ: speed doubles for a fixed mass. Momentum changes by?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Think V = ε − Ir.
cards.paper2Trap: Internal resistance is not necessarily rising.
cards.front: MCQ: a source emf is fixed and terminal p.d. drops as I rises. Why?
paper2Choices: The current has no effect on terminal p.d.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Gradient is vertical change divided by horizontal change: Δv/Δt.
cards.paper2Trap: Area gives displacement.
cards.front: MCQ: what does the gradient of a velocity-time graph measure?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: The gradient represents the rate of change of displacement: Δs/Δt.
cards.paper2Trap: Area has no simple standard AS meaning here.
cards.front: MCQ: what does the gradient of a displacement-time graph measure?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Integrate a over time.
cards.paper2Trap: Not displacement.
cards.front: MCQ: area under an acceleration-time graph gives?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Frequency is the reciprocal of period: f = 1/T. Look for inverse change.
cards.paper2Trap: Frequency and period are inversely related.
cards.front: MCQ: a wave period halves; frequency changes how?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Full λ corresponds to 2π.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not confuse 90° with π rad.
cards.front: MCQ: phase difference for a path difference λ/4?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: The whole pattern repeats every λ.
cards.paper2Trap: Adjacent nodes aren't one full wavelength apart.
cards.front: MCQ: distance between adjacent nodes of a stationary wave?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Particles separated by a node move oppositely.
cards.paper2Trap: Same loop is in phase, next loop out of phase.
cards.front: MCQ: phase difference between adjacent loops in a standing wave?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: At fixed μ and L, f ∝ √T.
cards.paper2Trap: Not four times.
cards.front: MCQ: a string's tension becomes 4 times larger. First harmonic frequency changes by?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Line separation is the reciprocal of lines per metre: d = 1/N.
cards.paper2Trap: A denser grating means smaller gaps.
cards.front: MCQ: the grating line density doubles; spacing d becomes?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Diffraction is greater for smaller aperture/λ ratio.
cards.paper2Trap: A wider slit gives a narrower pattern.
cards.front: MCQ: single-slit diffraction central maximum widens if slit width?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: For Young fringes, w = λD/s. Change only slit separation s in this expression.
cards.paper2Trap: A bigger slit separation doesn't widen fringes.
cards.front: MCQ: Young's slit separation doubles. Fringe spacing becomes?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Frequency is set by the source.
cards.paper2Trap: Reflected wavelength stays unchanged in same medium.
cards.front: MCQ: reflection at the same medium boundary changes frequency?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Polarisation requires transverse oscillations.
cards.paper2Trap: Longitudinal wave can still diffract.
cards.front: MCQ: longitudinal waves can be plane-polarised?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: The interface changes speed and wavelength.
cards.paper2Trap: Energy per photon doesn't change just at boundary.
cards.front: MCQ: light enters glass from air; which property remains constant?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Intercept on frequency axis is φ/h.
cards.paper2Trap: Slope remains h.
cards.front: MCQ: a higher work-function metal shifts the KEmax–frequency graph how?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: A half-wavelength path difference introduces a π-radian phase difference.
cards.paper2Trap: In phase at the sources doesn't imply in phase there.
cards.front: MCQ: at a point where two in-phase waves have λ/2 path difference, result?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Final minus initial, including signs.
cards.paper2Trap: Do not subtract speed magnitudes.
cards.front: MCQ: a ball changes velocity from +8 to −6 m/s. Δv?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Acceleration has become zero.
cards.paper2Trap: Drag is not zero.
cards.front: MCQ: an object falls at terminal speed. Resultant force?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Normal reaction = m(g−a).
cards.paper2Trap: Constant downward velocity gives mg, not less.
cards.front: MCQ: a lift accelerates down. Scale reading compared with mg?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Resolve later along chosen axes.
cards.paper2Trap: Weight isn't intrinsically parallel to the slope.
cards.front: MCQ: a free-body diagram on a slope needs weight in which direction?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Equal and opposite forces separated by distance.
cards.paper2Trap: A couple can still turn an object.
cards.front: MCQ: for two forces to form a couple, their resultant force is?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: KE = ½mv². At the same KE, speed is inversely proportional to √m.
cards.paper2Trap: Heavy doesn't mean faster at fixed energy.
cards.front: MCQ: at fixed kinetic energy, heavier particle speed is?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Force × distance.
cards.paper2Trap: The slope of F–x is spring constant only if Hooke's law holds.
cards.front: MCQ: a force–displacement graph area represents?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Pressure = F/A.
cards.paper2Trap: Pressure not proportional to area.
cards.front: MCQ: the pressure increases on a surface with fixed force when area?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Displacement is a vector.
cards.paper2Trap: Distance travelled is not zero.
cards.front: MCQ: a circular track route returns to start. Displacement?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: No external resultant impulse.
cards.paper2Trap: Kinetic energy need not be conserved.
cards.front: MCQ: two objects stick in a collision; which always conserved in isolated system?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Speed is |v|; inspect magnitude.
cards.paper2Trap: Negative velocity is direction, not speed reduction.
cards.front: MCQ: on a v-t graph, v becomes negative. Is the object necessarily slowing?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Force divided by area.
cards.paper2Trap: Stress isn't measured in newtons alone.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Strain is extension divided by original length, ΔL/L, so units cancel.
cards.paper2Trap: Length cancels.
cards.front: MCQ: strain has units?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: From Hooke's law F = kx, compare with the straight-line y = mx.
cards.paper2Trap: Area is elastic energy.
cards.front: MCQ: if a spring's force–extension graph straightens through origin, gradient is?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Impulse is fixed: Δp = F_average Δt. Divide by contact time.
cards.paper2Trap: Impulse remains the same.
cards.front: MCQ: if time of contact doubles with unchanged momentum change, average force?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: It is placed in series.
cards.paper2Trap: An infinite resistance would stop current.
cards.front: MCQ: ideal ammeter resistance?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: It is connected in parallel.
cards.paper2Trap: Zero resistance would short the branch.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.paper2Hint: Each branch spans the same two nodes.

cards.subject: Physics
